method: Full240 HAC(3) slope from ten-sample median blocks. Prior fixed z 2.291027529910169 and margin .0032. Three labels positive if lower>0, negative if upper<0, zero if interval within ±.0032, else unresolved. No future or truth lookahead; negative drift genuinely generated. Compare to positive-only SG049 rule projection, not entire SG049 warning-check pipeline.
assessment: Positive-only projection is not intended for true negative hypotheses. Three-way directional classifier correctly resolves 353 negative cases missed by projection, but also makes 32 new false directions versus projection. Do not present loss improvement as proof against a competitive ternary baseline. Correlated noise remains dominant source of errors.
limitations: Synthetic known families and observed samples only; no field deployment.
Original SG049 boundary warning check not reproduced in projection.
Loss weights are research choices and not real application stakes.
A strong direction-only classifier must test against a better ternary baseline and real negative-noise variations.
No benefit in sample counts; both fixed240.
next: SG051 directional uncertainty calibration: three-class confidence interval coverage and sign-error control, with explicit conservative ternary comparator and negative controls.
